verses.text: The whole earth was of one language and of one speech.
As they traveled east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they lived there.
They said to one another, “Come, let’s make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they used tar for mortar.
They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth.”
Yahweh came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men built.
Yahweh said, “Behold, they are one people, and they have all one language, and this is what they begin to do. Now nothing will be withheld from them, which they intend to do.
Come, let’s go down, and there confuse their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.”
So Yahweh scattered them abroad from there on the surface of all the earth. They stopped building the city.
Therefore its name was called Babel, because there Yahweh confused the language of all the earth. From there, Yahweh scattered them abroad on the surface of all the earth.
This is the history of the generations of Shem: Shem was one hundred years old when he became the father of Arpachshad two years after the flood.
Shem lived five hundred years after he became the father of Arpachshad, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Arpachshad lived thirty-five years and became the father of Shelah.
Arpachshad lived four hundred three years after he became the father of Shelah, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Shelah lived thirty years, and became the father of Eber.
Shelah lived four hundred three years after he became the father of Eber, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Eber lived thirty-four years, and became the father of Peleg.
Eber lived four hundred thirty years after he became the father of Peleg, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Peleg lived thirty years, and became the father of Reu.
Peleg lived two hundred nine years after he became the father of Reu, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Reu lived thirty-two years, and became the father of Serug.
Reu lived two hundred seven years after he became the father of Serug, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Serug lived thirty years, and became the father of Nahor.
Serug lived two hundred years after he became the father of Nahor, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and became the father of Terah.
Nahor lived one hundred nineteen years after he became the father of Terah, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Terah lived seventy years, and became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Now this is the history of the generations of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran became the father of Lot.
Haran died before his father Terah in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldees.
Abram and Nahor married wives. The name of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran who was also the father of Iscah.
Sarai was barren. She had no child.

Terah took Abram his son, Lot the son of Haran, his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram’s wife. They went from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan. They came to Haran and lived there.
The days of Terah were two hundred five years. Terah died in Haran.

footnotes.content: I remember how unity once was a blessing. One language, one speech - and yet in the days to come we would learn that shared words do not guarantee shared hearts turned to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They traveled east from where? From the mountains of Ararat no doubt, where Noah's family stepped off the ark. But even those who once knew God's covenant can begin to look for their own way, settling far from the worship they were meant to carry.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I notice how they said 'Come, let's...' to one another, banding together for their own purposes. There's nothing wrong with bricks, but when human hands work together to glorify themselves rather than God, even good things become a snare.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Look at their heart: they want a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and to make a name for themselves, lest they be scattered. In doing the very thing God had commanded after the flood - 'Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth' (Genesis 9:1, 7) - they feared scattering and built to stay. How our fear of God's word leads us to grasp at glory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Oh, what tenderness here. The God who made the heavens comes down to see. He doesn't send thunder from afar to begin - He stoops to look at the puny tower of man. Our great works look very small to the Lord, yet He still condescends to look upon us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh sees clearly what sin multiplies when united. One language gives them power to multiply their wickedness. I learn from this that unity apart from God is dangerous, but unity in Christ is our greatest blessing - for in Him our many tongues find one holy purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Come, let's go down' - the same gracious God who came down in verse 5 now comes down to act in mercy. Sometimes the kindest thing the Lord can do for proud hearts is to break our plans, so that we might turn to Him again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: So Yahweh scattered them abroad - the very thing they feared (v. 4). Our rebellions often carry their own punishment, yet even in judgment the faithfulness of God moves forward. The earth will be filled, just as He said it would.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo from Babel: our tongues still multiply confusion when pride rules us. Yet I am so grateful that through the risen Christ, by His Spirit, people of every tribe and language are brought into one family and will one day speak one song of praise. As of 2026-10, that hope steadies an old heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After the scattering of Babel, the Lord quietly returns to His faithful word. Through Shem's line, generation by generation, He preserves the seed through which blessing will come to all families of the earth (Genesis 12:3). I take comfort: when man builds monuments to himself, God is faithfully building the way of redemption.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here begins the story of Terah's family, and with it the turning of God's focus to one man, Abram. After tracing the nations, the Spirit narrows His gaze to show us the God who calls one family to bless all the families of the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Haran died before his father Terah, in Ur of the Chaldees. I wonder if that grief pressed heavily on Terah's heart. Yet the Lord, who numbers our days, was already at work to call Abram away from that place of sorrow to a place of promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sarai was Abram's wife, beautiful and beloved, yet barren (v. 30). It is a mercy of God that often the places of deepest lack become the very places where faith learns to rest wholly in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sarai was barren. She had no child. The Scripture states this plainly, and it matters. For it is through this barren woman that God will bring the One who would reverse the barrenness of many souls and open the way for the children of promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Terah took Abram, Sarai, and Lot and set out for Canaan, but they stopped at Haran and lived there. How often good intentions falter just short of obedience! Yet God's call to Abram will not be thwarted - in the next chapter, He will call him again to go on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Terah died in Haran at two hundred and five years. The chapter ends not with a monument to man's ambition, but with a grave. And from that grave, God's covenant mercy rises as He calls Abram forth to walk by faith to the land He will show him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
